resale_co.name: Certificate of Compliance for Sale of 1 or 2 Family Dwelling
resale_co.issued_by: Village of Ridgefield Park Building Department (Housing Inspector under the Construction Official)
resale_co.lead_time: File at least 12 days before closing (a higher fee applies after that). The application is reviewed and the certificate issued within 10 days.
resale_co.valid_for: Not transferable; if the change of occupancy does not happen within six months, a new application, inspection and certificate are needed.
requirements: Inspection confirms the home is legally occupied under the Village Zoning Code (1 family or 2 family)
Smoke alarms on each level and within 10 feet of each sleeping area (UL 217; battery or AC)
CO alarms (UL 2034, NFPA 720) in the immediate vicinity of sleeping rooms in homes with fuel-burning appliances or attached garages
Fire extinguisher in the kitchen of 1 and 2 family homes, 2A:10B:C, no more than 10 pounds, within 10 feet of the kitchen, top no more than 5 feet above the floor (code and form still list it)

Inspector also notes finished attic or basement, attic bathroom, basement kitchen or bath, exterior locks on bedroom doors, property maintenance (cut grass, shrubs, hedges) and a 4-inch house number visible from the street
Notarized acknowledgment signed by the owner/new owner (and tenant) that attics in two-story 1-2 family homes and basements may not be used as bedrooms or habitable space

fees.label: Certificate of compliance, application at least 12 days before the change of occupancy
fees.quote: Application submitted a minimum of 12 days prior to the scheduled change of occupancy, in the amount of $75.

fees.label: Application fewer than 12 days before the change of occupancy
fees.quote: Application submitted with fewer than 12 days prior to the scheduled change of occupancy, in the amount of $95.

fees.label: Reinspection
fees.quote: Reinspection fee shall be in the amount of $25.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Certificate of Compliance - Sale of 1 or 2 Family Dwelling (Building Department Forms & Applications page) and file it with the fee at the Building Department, 234 Main Street, Room 209, at least 12 days before closing. The same inspection covers smoke alarms, CO alarms and the extinguisher.
resale_co.contact_title: Construction Official (named on the application form)

evidence.quote: A certificate of compliance shall be required in all changes of occupancy in all residential dwelling units.

No person shall occupy or use any building or portion thereof for residential purposes, where the building or portion thereof has been sold by the owner or title to the premises has been transferred to another person, until the owner or an agent for the owner has applied for and secured a certificate of compliance from the Village of Ridgefield Park.
The application shall be filed at least 12 days prior to the anticipated date of closing, occurring in the case of resale, by the owner or agent for the owner.
If the change of occupancy specified in the application for a certificate of compliance does not occur within six months, a new application, inspection and certificate shall be required.
Before any change of occupancy, in any residential dwelling unit, a Certificate of Compliance must be obtained from the Building Department.
Application for Certificate of Compliance - Sale of 1 of 2 Family Dwelling (PDF)
APPLICATION FOR CERTIFICATE OF COMPLIANCE FOR SALE OF 1 OR 2 FAMILY DWELLING

resale_co.notes: Chapter 153 of the Village code (amended in its entirety 2-14-2006 by Ord. 06-03) was read in full through the ecode360 print view. The posted application is a scanned image with no text layer, so its wording cannot be machine checked; it names Construction Official Michael Landolfi and a gmail address (Mikebuilding@gmail.com), which is not used here as the official email. The packet also includes a Fire Prevention letter asking new owners to say whether they will rent the home; non-owner-occupied 1-2 family rentals must register with the Bureau of Fire Prevention (rental-only). Tax searches must carry a notice that a certificate of compliance is required for resale.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level and within 10 feet of each sleeping area (NFPA 74 placement, UL 217; battery or AC powered)
CO alarms (UL 2034, NFPA 720; battery, hardwired or plug-in) in the immediate vicinity of all sleeping rooms, no more than 10 feet away, in homes with fuel-burning appliances or attached garages

Fire extinguisher 2A:10B:C, no more than 10 pounds, manufacturer's bracket, within 10 feet of the kitchen, top no more than 5 feet above the floor; serviced and tagged within 12 months or a recent purchase receipt (code and form still list it)

authorities.name: Village of Ridgefield Park Building Department (Certificate of Compliance covers smoke/CO; Bureau of Fire Prevention is the fire code agency)
authorities.lead_time: File at least 12 days before closing for the lower fee. Certificate valid six months for the stated change of occupancy.

fees.quote: Application submitted with fewer than 12 days prior to the scheduled change of occupancy, in the amount of $95.

authorities.how_to_apply: The smoke alarm, CO alarm and extinguisher check is part of the Building Department's Certificate of Compliance inspection; there is no separate fire application for a 1-2 family sale. File the Certificate of Compliance application at 234 Main Street, Room 209.
authorities.contact_title: Building Department; Fire Official Peter A. Danzo (pdanzo@ridgefieldpark.org, (201) 440-2570) heads the Bureau of Fire Prevention

evidence.quote: Existing Buildings - Before any change of occupancy may take place, a Certificate of Smoke Detector and CO Detector Compliance shall be obtained from the Village Building Department.
All residential occupancies are now required to have Carbon Monoxide Detectors installed as well as Smoke Detectors, before a certificate can be issued.
to ensure that, at a minimum, battery-operated smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are installed and that each kitchen of one- and two-family dwellings contains a proper fire extinguisher.

fire_cert.notes: In Ridgefield Park the single Certificate of Compliance from the Building Department serves as both the resale certificate and the smoke/CO certificate; the state fire directory also lists the Building Department as the smoke detector compliance office, while the Bureau of Fire Prevention (50 Main Street) is the fire code agency and handles multiple dwellings. Fees are the same three code fees shown under the resale certificate. The Village code and form still require a kitchen fire extinguisher, which state law (P.L.2025, c.19) dropped from the sale certificate in February 2025; confirm with the Building Department.

other_items.label: Attic and basement occupancy affidavit
other_items.detail: Buyers (and any tenants) sign a notarized acknowledgment that attics in two-story 1-2 family homes may not be habitable space and basements may not be bedrooms.

other_items.label: Rental registration letter
other_items.detail: New owners return a Fire Prevention letter saying whether they will rent the home; non-owner-occupied 1-2 family homes must register with the Bureau of Fire Prevention (rental-only).
